chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Dagan and discovering Olga San Juan for the Copacabana
summary: Manager Dagan wanted a lead for the Copacabana chorus, and Machito recommended young Olga San Juan, whom a scout then hired.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Okay. What else do you remember about Los Angeles? How did Bing Crosby and Nino Remay get into that picture with you?
Well, because Olga San Juan, I knew Olga San Juan when she was a baby.
The Puerto Rican actress that went and made it big in Hollywood.
Edmund O'Brien. So is a, you know, nice story and I don't want to brag about myself, but it was an accident, let's say. My personal manager was Dagan, that he was like a right hand of Paul Whiteman.
Dagan - D a g a n - Dagan. He was from Colombia

and he was like a contact man for Paul Whiteman and one day we was working at La Conga and he liked, you know, the sound that we had and he say: "Machito, I am going to book you, I am going to be your personal manager". I said okay, so he got me into The Great White Way. He got me into a different club; so he was looking for a leading lady.

The time was - Carmen Miranda was in her heyday and they were looking for a leading lady for the chorus girls of Copacabana, and this girl, Olga San Juan, was taking lessons, Spanish dancing. She could sing in Spanish and fake Portuguese. So he told me that he needed a nice-looking girl that it could front the Copacabana chorus girls; so he says: "If you know anybody with a nice complexion--beautiful--bring her over". So, I just - it just come to mind, Gee, Olga San Juan fitted this picture. So Olga San Juan used to live in 111th and 5th Ave., in top of that bar, remember? One flight up, next to the Hispanic Theatre. So I went up there and talked to her and to the father - because she was about fifteen years old - if she was particularly interested to work, because she was going to high school, and the father was hesitant. So we made some kind of deal that she made the first show and the second show, not the third show. So the first show was eight or eight-thirty and the second show was eleven-thirty; so she always got home early.
So one scout saw her dancing and singing at the Copacabana and for what he saw and he hired her to go to Columbia, Columbia pictures, for a tryout.
